replacements.reference: Guapo, a named bull in Ferdinand
replacements.fit: The proud mouth, cool brows, googly eyes, and pink field suit the handsome but comic bravado of Guapo.

replacements.reference: Bones, the agile bull in Ferdinand
replacements.fit: The skateboard, scattered-room backdrop, raised eyes, and nervous smile give this bull a nimble underdog quality.

replacements.reference: Valiente, the competitive bull in Ferdinand
replacements.fit: The smug face and intense red-green swamp spiral project the theatrical confidence of Valiente.
Devon is a natural male name that keeps the calm round-eyed portrait human and avoids leaning on the hamburger prop.
The scarlet field, angry face, scream, bat, and ball create an explosive action silhouette worthy of Asteroid.
The tilted eyes, red lollipop, blue field, and mad mouth give Woopaa the right strange, punchy collectible energy.
The dark complexion, droopy expression, and soccer prop suit a sturdy surname-like cattle name rather than another tool word.
The hard glare, mad mouth, purple field, and broad horns call for a powerful bull-breed name.
Jersey keeps the laughing googly-eyed portrait light, approachable, and name-like instead of mechanical.

replacements.reference: ProRodeo Hall of Fame bull Red Rock
replacements.fit: The red sunset field, proud mouth, blue eyes, and dark face make Redrock a direct color-and-famous-bull match.
The sunny backlight, bright smile, and pale face give the compact rugged Aubrac name an upbeat storybook feel.
The dark face, horns, playful eyes, and soccer ball fit the compact strength of a Brangus bull.
Angry brows, closed eyes, a scream, and an overgrown landscape give Bushwacker an exact fierce wilderness fit.
The warm dark face, laughing mouth, brown eyes, and pink background suit Bonsmara's rounded fantasy-name rhythm.
The long beard, grey stare, brush, and prominent horns make Highland the strongest whole-portrait breed match.

replacements.reference: Historic Durham or Shorthorn cattle breed name
replacements.fit: The happy mustache, warm complexion, and scarlet background suit a sturdy, natural Western surname-name.
The cheerful face, sun disk, and bright lollipop favor a friendly place-name breed over a machine term.

replacements.reference: ProRodeo Hall of Fame bucking bull Bodacious
replacements.fit: The dark face, angry brows, grimace, red field, and soccer ball produce the batch's boldest championship-bull portrait.
Green stretched eyes, a heart sunrise, and a mad mouth create the strange magical tension that Voodoo captures.

replacements.reference: Three-time PBR World Champion Bull Little Yellow Jacket
replacements.fit: The yellow lollipop, wink, white cloud, and violet sky make Jacket a playful literal-color echo without becoming a food joke.
The tan face, happy eyes, tense mouth, white cloud, and soccer ball favor a short athletic breed name.
The beer glass, laughing mouth, dark face, and purple field give Panhandle a relaxed rodeo-bar Western identity.
The grey stare and sad beard make Murray Grey's human-sounding first component a subtle portrait match that ignores the hamburger.
The tight eyes, restrained smile, and overgrown landscape suit a rangy cattle name with movement and character.
The sun, red-wine prop, dark complexion, and calm face align with a warm-climate red-cattle reference.

replacements.reference: Maquina, the silent bull in Ferdinand
replacements.fit: The long beard, surprised face, brush-like ice cream prop, and scarlet field create a strange engineered-character look.
The scream and dense overgrown wasteland make Droughtmaster read like both a real breed and an RPG-style title.
The happy mustache and sideways stare give Dillinger a mature outlaw-name quality while avoiding the burger prop.

replacements.reference: PBR World Champion Bull Mossy Oak Mudslinger
replacements.fit: The raised bat, wide smile, scarlet background, and diamond-sized surname energy make Mudslinger livelier and less generic than Tornado.
The dark face, basketball, tight spiral, and worried expression benefit from a short friendly name with an unmistakable bovine route.
The pale face, compact mustache, tight happy eyes, and violet field echo the light-colored breed and give the long name elegance.

replacements.reference: Three-time PBR World Champion Bull Smooth Operator
replacements.fit: The happy eyes, basketball, red spiral, and controlled mad mouth make Smooth an ironic but memorable champion-bull call name.
The pale face, pink cloud field, ice cream, and laugh favor an airy place-name breed rather than a structural term.
Blue doll eyes, a bright smile, and an overgrown landscape make Piedmont feel pastoral and naturally character-like.

replacements.reference: PBR World Champion Bull Ridin Solo
replacements.fit: The solitary moon, beer glass, proud mouth, and round eyes give Solo a clean nighttime saloon-story fit.
The scarlet field, red rose, sun, dark face, and winking eye make the red-cattle breed route unusually literal.
The fire background, dark complexion, angry brows, and beard need a strong heat-country cattle name.
The dark face, soccer ball, googly eyes, and grimace suit a compact athletic surname-like breed name.
The coin, happy eyes, laugh, and overgrown landscape make Nelore sound adventurous and valuable without using a tool name.
The pale face, laughing mouth, beer glass, and pink field suit a short, easygoing island-breed name.
The angry brows, drink prop, overgrown setting, and bright pink field give Ongole a tough but melodic contrast.

replacements.reference: Ben, the fatherly bull in Barnyard
replacements.fit: Ben is deliberately human and reassuring for the calm mustached portrait, preventing the hamburger from creating an uncomfortable food-animal name.
The closed eyes, laugh, soccer ball, and bright red field support an energetic alpine-breed name with unusual collectability.
